summary.root_cause_text: Payment provider internal://payments-v1 times out on every call, so orders are marked processed without payment. Config and deploys look normal, and no available tool can fix the provider itself. The deeper cause is unknown.
recommended: A human should investigate or restore the payment provider's availability, or its network path.
Once payments succeed, run reprocess_orders all_unpaid (it never double-charges).
Consider pausing order intake until the provider recovers.
Add alerting on payment provider timeouts, which are logged only at DEBUG.

The URL itself matches the known-good config, so the timeout must be coming from somewhere else—I should check the config logs for clues.
No log lines at DEBUG or above from config.
No log lines at DEBUG or above from admin.

The provider is timing out despite config being v1, so maybe the worker is holding a stale config. Restarting the worker would process the empty queue safely, but new orders could go unpaid in the meantime—so I'll first try setting the config to the same value as the smallest, safest step.
payment_provider_url: 'internal://payments-v1' -> 'internal://payments-v1'. Confirmed: the service is now using the new value.

Still broken:
- [business] payment_gap: 60 of 73 orders were processed but have no payment.
This looks like an outage on the provider's end, which no tool can resolve—reprocessing wouldn't help either. A worker restart seems unlikely to fix it too, so escalation is the right move.
